notes.decision: Translated 'shines forth in the Sweetness.' ⲧⲣⲓ̈ⲉ tentatively read as a verb related to ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate' (cf. ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' in glossary). ⲡⲭⲗⲥⲉ per accumulated vocabulary = 'sweetness' (Lyc. for ϩⲗⲟϭ); functions here as cosmological locus = the Land of Sweetness/Light. Could alternatively represent ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height' with intrusive ⲗ; either reading yields a divine-realm locative.

Rendered 'performing the fourth (watch).' ϩⲧⲟⲉ per accumulated vocab = 'fourth, quarter (of night).' The phrase remains opaque without more context — the Two Sons / Living Soul performing some quartered cosmic office.

Translated 'furnace.' Unattested lexeme; reading from context (sun-ship simile + 'the great Spirit dwells within') requires a glowing/contained vessel. Possibly related to ⲃⲣⲏⲣⲉ 'kiln' (Crum) or a Lycopolitan variant. The image is the sun-ship as a great fiery container with the Spirit blazing within.

Translated 'dwells.' Verbal stem unidentified; possibly = ⲱϣ qualitative (be poured forth, abide) with prosthetic ⲍ-, or related to a verb of containment/blazing. The cosmological context is the great Spirit's indwelling presence within the cosmic vessel.
Per accumulated vocabulary: 'unto the foot of' = supervisory/rescue arrival into someone's presence. Here describes the warrior-man entering the captive prince's place to free him.

Translated 'yet again.' Phrase unattested; possibly a Lycopolitan compound adverb meaning 'at this moment also' or a discourse-marker introducing a follow-up teaching. Functionally parallel to ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ.

Two parallel agentive compounds: 'choosers' (ⲣⲉϥ-ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄) and 'redeemers' (ⲣⲉϥ-ⲥⲱⲧⲉ). The disciples are exhorted to be both selectors and redeemers of their own souls — paralleling the apostle's two functions.

Tentatively rendered 'impassibility.' Best parsed as Greek ἀπάθεια / ἀπαθής 'without passion, impassible' adapted to Coptic with -ⲏⲧ ending. The phrase '[impassibility?] of the eyes of the light' fits a Manichaean spiritual register. Alternative: a native compound on -ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' (e.g. ⲁⲧ-ϩⲏⲧ).

Variant orthography of ⲡⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ (accumulated vocabulary: 'wellspring/source of all evil'). The ⲝ for ⲭ is a known Lycopolitan/Coptic alternation. Translated 'wellspring of all the powers' — the King of Darkness as the source-fountain of the dark host.

Translated 'imprint.' From ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, stamp, imprint.' The five likenesses in the King of Darkness's body correspond to the imprint of the five archonic creature-kinds of the five worlds — a typological correspondence: each body-part of the Dark King IS the seal/imprint of a class of dark creatures.

'His head' — Lycopolitan reflex with epenthetic ϩ. Standard correspondence in this schema: head of King of Darkness = lion = world of fire. Note this differs slightly from the line-13 sequence on page 41 (head/lion = world of fire here, vs. some earlier lists). Five-fold correspondence: head→lion→fire; wings/shoulders→eagle→wind; hands/feet→demons→smoke; belly→dragon→darkness; loins→fish→water (the last to be restored).

Translated 'his loins/hindquarters.' In the standard Manichaean five-fold body schema of the King of Darkness, after head/wings/hands-feet/belly the fifth body-part is the loins or tail, corresponding to fish = world of water. The lacuna at the end of the line would have completed 'is in the form of [a fish, according to the likeness of the world of water].'
